6926.html:
6926 nagná 'naked' RV., nágnaka- AV. [In mngs. 'shameless, wanton (cf. nagnā́-), small boy or girl' poss. influenced by, or influencing, 'defective' words (e.g. *lakka-, *liṅga-²), cf. lagnikā- (lex.) ~ nagnikā- (MBh.) 'young girl'. — See Add.]
    Pa. nagga-, naggiyā- f., Pk. ṇagga-, ṇagiṇa-; Gy. eur. naṅo, nango 'naked', arm. nəgal- 'to unclothe', as. nangoldi; Bshk. nΛn 'naked', Phal. nāano (nāl-po 'barefoot'), Sh.gil. nánŭ, koh. gur. nonŭ, K. nonᵘ, S. naṅgu, °go, L. P. naṅgā, WPah.bhal. nago; Ku. nā̃g, nāṅ 'nakedness', nāgṛo, nāṅṛo 'naked', nāgo 'a class of ascetics', gng. nāg 'naked'; N. nāṅgo 'naked', nāgo 'debauched or wanton soldier', naṅginu 'to be uncovered'; OB. lāga 'naked', B. nāṅgā, nāṅā, neṅaṭ, neṅṭā; Or. naṅg(h)ā, laṅghā 'naked, unsheathed', naṅgaḷā, la° 'naked', naṅguḷī, la° 'naked ascetic', nāgā 'a class of naked ascetics'; Mth. nā̃gaṭ 'naked', Bhoj. nāgā, laṅā; H. nãg, nãgā, nãgṭā 'naked', nãgiyānā 'to strip', nāgā m. 'naked mendicant'; G. nāgũ 'naked', nāgṛũ 'naked, lean, shameless'; M. nāgā, nāgḍā, nākṭā, nāgvā 'naked', naṅgā 'penniless' (← H.); Ko. nāgḍo 'naked'. — In additions to dissimilations shown above the word 'naked' was liable to various deformations: Pk. ṇigiṇa-, Ash. nutuṛíṅ, lu°; Wg. nĩgiṭi 'in want' (cf. B. leṅaṭ 'naked' s.v. *liṅga-²), nitoṅ (< *niktāṅga- ?), nipteŕε῀ 'naked', Pr. ninǰē̃yigi; — poss. < *niṣṭrāṇa-: Dm. nic̣íṇ, Kal. liṣṭän, Gaw. niċhāṅg, Sv. niċaṅ.
    nagnā́-; *nagnapadara-, *nagnāṅga-; *unnagna-.
    Addenda: nagná- [Dial. ā ~ a < apophonic IE. o (cf. IE. *nogʷnó- ~ Hit. nekumant- 'naked') T. Burrow BSOAS xxxviii 70]
    WPah.kṭg. naṅgɔ 'naked', J. nāṅgā, Garh. nā̃gu; — Garh. nɔni (or < *nānna- ?) 'small girl'.
